segmentation.text: intending to turn to the left
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
and having given a signal when and as required,
and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: "a vehicle": the left-turning road user t, other than ego, of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "The driver" read through its controlled motion.
"within an intersection": t's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the intersection i (st.intersection); i is the region t's intention is declared at.

"having given a signal": t showed a left signal, its turn indicator state left (sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ... left') or an arm signal of meaning left (sig.hand_signal), at some observation since t occupied its approach carrier into i; the signal itself, not a declared intention, and not the turn. "when and as required": the timing and manner another statute sets, outside this corpus; the signal is read as given before the judged observation.

"may make such left turn": t is making the left turn it intends, drv.motion.turning_left (moving with its heading turning to the left at or above the yaw tolerance), a turn under way rather than one completed.

"the drivers of all other vehicles": ego, a vehicle (admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) other than t, its driver read through its controlled motion. "approaching the intersection": ego occupies a carrier c_e whose entrance end is i and does not overlap i, or enters i from it (st.lane_enters, rel.occupies). "from the opposite direction": c_e and the carrier from which t entered i carry opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), as rel.oncoming's contract directs, not the current headings.
"shall yield": granting precedence (DEF-NRS-484A-210 "unless one grants precedence to the other"): ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest) or not in conflict with t (operationalization of f15).
"the vehicle making the left turn": the same t, turning left (drv.motion.turning_left) at the judged observation.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 "approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other"
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: two road users are in conflict where, projected at their current velocities, their centres approach within the time-to-collision horizon and their closest-approach centre distance is below the clearance at which their bodies would touch. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the projected velocities and positions.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes turning left at the target region.

applicability: Ego is a vehicle (driven: agency reading) approaching an intersection i (on a carrier c_e whose entrance end is i, not overlapping i, or entering i from it), and some vehicle t other than ego overlaps i, declares int.left_turn at i, is turning left (drv.motion.turning_left, p.turn_yaw_tolerance, p.rest_speed_tolerance), showed a left signal (sig.turn_indicator left or sig.hand_signal left) at some observation since it occupied its approach carrier into i, has complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 (t as its ego) at every observation since it entered i, and entered i from a carrier c_t whose direction and c_e's have a dot product below minus p.opposite_direction_tolerance (st.lane_direction).
obligation: Ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, p.rest_speed_tolerance) or not in conflict with t: not both prim.closest_approach_within(ego, t) with horizon p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(ego, t) with the same horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the drivers' are read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Vehicle t, within the intersection with int.left_turn and its left indicator on since its approach, waited while no oncoming vehicle was close and now turns left. Ego approaches from the opposite direction and keeps moving; their projected closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; ego slows and comes to rest at the edge of the intersection until t completes its turn.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: t crosses the intersection straight ahead (no int.left_turn, not turning left); ego approaches from the opposite direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Scene of forbid, but the source declares sig.turn_indicator and sig.hand_signal absent: whether t signalled cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but t's indicator stayed off and it gave no arm signal: t gave no signal, so the opposing drivers' duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but t began its turn while ego was already within the immediate-hazard distance of the intersection: t did not yield as NRS_484B_253_o1 requires, so the duty to yield to it does not arise.

param_proposals.name: p.rest_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-detection noise floor: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement, set at the resolution of the speed measurement so that a complete cessation from movement is recognized despite sensor jitter.
param_proposals.source: Naturalistic-driving and simulator stop-detection practice (SHRP 2 event coding; CARLA ground-truth velocity resolution).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a projected approach of the centres within this time counts toward the danger of a crash.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Hyden (1987) Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique; van der Horst (1990) TTC thresholds.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the projected closest approach below which the bodies of two passenger vehicles would touch or nearly touch (about a half-length plus a half-width of a design passenger car).
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, design vehicle P dimensions.

param_proposals.name: p.opposite_direction_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which two approach directions still count as opposite (thirty degrees), covering skewed approaches.
param_proposals.source: Trajectory-processing conventions for opposing-movement classification at intersections (inD).

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Yaw rate below which a change of heading counts as none: above lane-keeping yaw noise, below the yaw rates of turning at a junction.
param_proposals.source: Vehicle-dynamics practice for turn-onset detection from yaw-rate sensors.
